key_insight: The apparent triage failures come from how the model maps its preserved clinical understanding to constrained multiple-choice answers, not from a loss of medical representation.
clinical_relevance: For AI triage tools, the output format can meaningfully change safety performance, so evaluation should test both free-text and forced-choice settings.
method: Sparse autoencoder (SAE) features were compared in Gemma 3 4B/12B IT and Qwen3-8B across free-text and multiple-choice triage prompts.
Three analyses were combined: natural-language autoencoder verbalization, decision-token logit attribution, and top-feature characterization.
Behavioral checks included option-order shuffling and analysis of off-by-one acuity mistakes.
evidence_signal: Across the same clinical narratives, medical features stayed active in the shared context but went silent at the multiple-choice decision token, while scaffold and format features dominated the logits.
watch_item: This result is about benchmarked prompt/output behavior in specific models, so it should not be taken as a guarantee of real-world triage safety or generalized clinical reliability.
paper_title: Internal Representation, Not Clinical Knowledge: Where Apparent LLM Triage Failures Originate
